subject: Inquiry on Integrating multinomPois with Distance Sampling in Double Observer Data

messages.author: 5f360b7a2b206a40
messages.subject: Inquiry on Integrating multinomPois with Distance Sampling in Double Observer Data
parts:
I am reaching out to seek expert advice regarding the integration of multinomPois function with distance sampling in the context of my ongoing research.

My study involves five years of count data using a double observer approach. Notably, our observations were not simultaneous but conducted within short time intervals from one another. This methodology was chosen due to the nature of our system: (1) The 2nd observer collected habitat characteristics (%cover at 50m radius at point) after first observer made observations and the ruggedness of the terrain (alpine) between points (250m apart) and (2) this species (Rosy-Finch), is frequently found in close proximity to nest habitat (breeding season surveys; cliffs) and forages close to snow-covered areas, thus making it relatively visible.

Each point count was conducted over seven-minute intervals, divided into three discrete segments: 0-3 minutes, 3:01-5 minutes, and 5:01-7 minutes. During these counts, we recorded both the group size (clusters of individuals vs. solitary bird) and the total number of individuals observed at each point (e.g count). Each observation of Rosy-Finch, a distance and direction were taken with precision (laser range finder). 

In light of this, I am particularly interested in understanding if the multinomPois function for single-season data can be effectively combined with the distsamp function. Our primary goal is to estimate both the detection probability and abundance, taking into consideration the distance sampling aspect. Further, I have 5 years of this data where each point was visited by both observers at least 3x to 5x (2018-2022); Once per year by both observers for at least 3 years. 

To provide further context, our research aligns with the abundance models described in the unmarked framework, where different combinations of sampling methods and temporal structures (I believe the assumptions are met here for the discrete-time bins mentioned above) are utilized. We are exploring models similar to those outlined by Royle et al. (2004) and Buckland et al. (2001), especially those integrating detection and abundance estimation.

I have read through "Applied Hierarchical Modeling in Ecology" Vol 1 Kéry & Royle and cannot find if this modeling will work outside of the n-mixture approach. Given the specific characteristics of our study species and the methodology employed, your insights on whether the multinomPois function can accommodate distance sampling data in our scenario would be invaluable! Any guidance or suggestions on how to approach this analysis using unmarked would be greatly appreciated.

Also - is it possible to integrate groups (clusters) and count into this framework? Ofthen between Observer 1 and Observer 2, our count data was very similar even between time intervals of several hours, and group size numbers (e.g. a cluster of 3 male finches foraging on snow) would be seen by both observers; different exact positions, but somewhere on the same snow patch or an adjacent one. 

Best,

Tim

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: Inquiry on Integrating multinomPois with Distance Sampling in Double Observer Data
parts:
Hi Tim,

It sounds like you have double-observer, time removal (based on your time bins - could the same bird be counted in multiple time bins? it isn't clear) and distance sampling data. The gdistremoval() function can fit a model to a combination of time removal and distance sampling data. unmarked does not support simultaneously handling double-observer+time removal+distance sampling, or double-observer + distance sampling, although either of these should be possible with e.g. JAGS or nimble. Furthermore I am not sure if your non-simultaneous double observer data would meet the assumptions of the double-observer model in multinomPois in general. I suspect it doesn't, but I could be wrong. Maybe someone else on the list has considered it.

Ken

parts:
Dr. Kellner (Ken) et al., 

Great to get a response from you and thank you for the insights! I was reading your recent pub in Methods in EE - so well written and clear, thank you.

I would like to clarify some aspects of my research and seek further guidance. In my study, I have been focusing on testing double observer and detection probability using MRDS, primarily concentrating on detection rather than abundance. Now, I'm exploring the use of unmarked for comparative purposes. To address your concern, I can confirm that in our methodology, the same bird is not counted twice across different time bins.

Your paper and the last section of chapter 9 in Kéry & Royle's book on "ADVANCED HIERARCHICAL DISTANCE SAMPLING", specifically 9.4.3 "Remarks" regarding DO/DS (with group size and SCR), piqued my interest in the time removal method. Could you advise on how best to integrate this method with the double observer data in unmarked?

Additionally, I'm working with single-season data collected over five seasons. I would appreciate any recommendations on approaches or specific models within unmarked that are ideally suited for analyzing multi-season single-observation data. Regarding the double-observer aspect of our study, is there a way to incorporate the observations of two different observers within the distsamp function as a variable? Also, I'm curious about the possibility of including group size and count data in the analysis. Does unarked have the capability to handle these aspects?

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: Inquiry on Integrating multinomPois with Distance Sampling in Double Observer Data
parts:
Hi Tim,

unmarked doesn't have a way to integrate double observer data with distance sampling at this time, the way mrds does. Nor does it explicitly handle group size. I'd like to do that someday. I think if you want to use unmarked right now, your choices are:

1) Use the distance sampling data alone (distsamp)
2) Use the double observer data or removal data alone (multinomPois)
3) Use the combination of removal data and distance sampling data (gdistremoval). See https://academic.oup.com/auk/article/131/4/476/5149376 for an overview of this model.

Then the next choice is how to handle the temporal structure. The main choices here would be

1) "Stack" each combination of site and year and treat the site-years as independent sites, and then use the appropriate single season model (distsamp, multinomPois, gdistremoval).  You could fit a site-level random effect to account for pseudoreplicating across sites in this situation, all three of these functions support this. Search the listserv for "stacking" to see many discussion of this approach. This approach works better if you want to estimate some kind of temporal trend in abundance.
2) Fit a properly dynamic model estimating recruitment, survival, etc between years. You can do this with distsampOpen (using only distance sampling data) or multmixOpen (using only double observer or removal data). See the references in the help files of these functions for details of these models.

Ken
